B_0001.why: Vital Strategies “India - Tobacco Control – Main Bhi Sunita (Sunita 2.0) - Hindi”, 30 sec. Sunita, the wife of a cancer victim, speaks: "मेरे पति 18 साल की उम्र से खैनी खाया करते थे… उन्हें कैंसर नाम की खतरनाक बीमारी हो गई है". She says he is the only earner and she cannot sleep thinking about the future: "खैनी ने हमारी जिंदगी बर्बाद कर दी". The voiceover then says "खैनी, गुटका, जर्दा, पान मसाला परिवार तबाह करते हैं, तंबाकू आज ही छोड़ें" and gives the helpline, "सहायता के लिए 1800112356 पर कॉल करें". The description says it was launched in 17 languages by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India, for airing in TV programmes and films from 10 August 2024. The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and urges quitting. It does not make any product attractive.

B_0002.why: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare “A short anti-tobacco video on passive smoke”, 38 sec. The description says it shows how indirect or passive smoking is ruining the lives of people around you, and ends with “Quit smoking”. The English voiceover says “smoking can cost you your health and can also seriously affect the health and welfare of those around you”, then “don’t have them pay the price for your smoking”, and ends with “smoking will cost you”. The main message warns about harm to the smoker and to others, and encourages quitting. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

B_0003.why: Vital Strategies “India - Tobacco Control - When You Quit - Hindi”, 30 sec, part of India’s anti-tobacco campaign. The Hindi voiceover says the study shows that "धूम्रपान छोड़ने के 20 मिनट बाद आपका रक्तचाप सामान्य हो जाता है", that nicotine in the body falls within days, and that within 12 months the "हृदय रोग का खतरा भी आधा रह जाता है". It then warns about the damage smoking does now and ends with "तंबाकू आज ही छोड़ें, मदद के लिए कॉल करें" and the quitline number. The main message supports quitting and warns about harm. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

B_0004.why: “Disclaimer || Akshay Kumar || New 2018 || smoking Is Injured To Health”, 64 sec, uploaded by “IVY Bhojpuri Gaana”. It is a film-style anti-smoking spot. In one frame a man smokes a cigarette on a house verandah while another man in a white shirt looks on. At about 30 seconds a hand holds up a cigarette pack with a graphic health warning that reads “WARNING Smoking kills”. Other frames show men talking and reacting, and the video ends on a channel logo. The title presents it as the anti-smoking disclaimer. The main message warns about the harm of smoking and discourages use. It does not make any cigarette brand attractive

B_0005.why: Anti-tobacco campaign spot “Shadow” (India), 33 sec, posted by Vital Strategies and issued in public interest by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, with the National Tobacco Control Programme. A man smokes on a railway-station bench while a woman and two children near him cough and look unwell, with smoke stains spreading on the boy’s chest. The English voiceover says “when you smoke so did the people around you, it can irritate their eyes, bring on asthma attacks and even chest pains”, and “your smoke can cause their lung cancer”. It ends on a “Tobacco Kills – QUIT TODAY” card. The main message warns about the harm of smoking, including second-hand smoke, and urges quitting. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

B_0006.why: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare anti-tobacco PSA “India - Sunita (Hindi) - Testimonial”, 31 sec, posted by Vital Strategies. Sunita, a 27-year-old wife and mother, speaks about oral cancer after using smokeless tobacco. The on-screen Hindi text and voiceover say "मैंने कब सोचा था मेरी जिंदगी यूं बदल जाएगी… तंबाकू ने सब कुछ बदल दिया… अब इस फैलते हुए कैंसर को मेरे चेहरे से काटना पड़ेगा". The video shows her holding a wedding photo, then a graphic surgery scene, then her face after the operation. The closing line says "खैनी, गुटखा, तंबाकू, जर्दा, पान मसाला आपका जीवन उजाड़ देते हैं", and the end card reads "तंबाकू जानलेवा है, आज ही छोड़ो". The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and urges quitting. It does not make any product attractive.

B_0007.why: Anti-tobacco testimonial “India - Mukesh: Smokeless Tobacco Campaign (Hindi)”, 34 sec, posted by Vital Strategies and filmed at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai. A doctor’s voiceover says "हम रोज 50 नए मरीज देख रहे हैं… 80 से 90 प्रतिशत मुंह के कैंसर तंबाकू चबाने से होते हैं". The video shows Mukesh Harane in a hospital bed with a feeding tube and graphic close-ups of his face, saying "मेरा नाम मुकेश है… अब मुझे कैंसर हुआ है… शायद मैं बोल नहीं सकूंगा". A caption notes his death. The narrator says "अफसोस, मुकेश बच नहीं सका और वो सिर्फ 24 साल का था", then lists "खैनी, पान, गुटका", and the video ends on a black card reading "तम्बाकू जानलेवा है". The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and discourages use. It does not make any product attractive.

A_0001.why: “Rajnigandha Pan Masala Hindi 30 Second Ad - Kinetic Energy Tiles”, 30 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel. A Rajnigandha logo shows throughout. The story shows a successful man whose footsteps power kinetic energy tiles that light a village, with the subtitle "यह पावर है बढ़ते कदमों की" and "जो कदम जमीन से जुड़े करेंगे इस डिश को रोशन". In the closing scene a man holds a Rajnigandha tin and appears to eat from it, smiling. The ad ends on a pack shot of “Rajnigandha Flavoured Pan Masala” with the tagline “Kuch Kar Aisa, Duniya Banna Chahe Tere Jaisa”, and the voiceover names the brand. The main message links the pan masala brand to success and positive change. It makes the brand attractive and shows the product being consumed. A small on-screen line at the bottom right does not change this, so I labelled it promotional.

A_0002.why: “DSGroup - Rajnigandha Pan Masala, Glfer Edit, 30 sec”, about 33 sec, uploaded by the brand’s channel (RajnigandhaPM). It is a golf-themed brand film about “success that inspires”. It shows a golfer swinging before a cheering crowd, a trophy presentation, and a golfer in a red cap, with the Hindi subtitles "तू मुझसे आगे जरूर है…", "शुक्रगुजार हूं मैं तेरा, एक तेरे पीछे चलते चलते मैं कितनों से आगे निकल गया". It ends with a pack shot of the “Rajnigandha Flavoured Pan Masala” tin and the tagline "कुछ कर ऐसा, दुनिया बनना चाहे तेरे जैसा". The main message links the pan masala brand with success, sport and inspiration, so it makes the brand attractive. A tiny line of on-screen text does not change that, so I labelled it promotional.

A_0003.why: “Vimal Elaichi - Ajay Devgn | Shahrukh Khan | Akshay Kumar I Hindi TVC 45 secs”, 45 sec, uploaded by the brand’s channel (Vimal Elaichi). A stylish star-led film with three men in a white convertible, a call up to a woman on a balcony, and red saffron-like particles falling through the scenes. The Hindi subtitles include "ओए नीचे आ, घोड़े बेच दिए क्या" and "केसरिया के दीवाने", and it ends with a Vimal Elaichi pack shot and the slogan "बोलो जुबाँ केसरी". The title names the three film stars. The main message makes the brand attractive through celebrity glamour and a catchy slogan, so I labelled it promotional. I saw no health warning, only small text saying the saffron shown is a creative depiction.

A_0004.why: “Raj Niwas Pan Masala TVC 30 secs”, about 30 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel (Raj Niwas Pan Masala). A glamorous royal-style film: a palace and gardens, a man in a dark suit and a woman in an embellished dress on a veranda, two riders on horseback, and a car scene where a hand holds the sachet with the line “Maharaja ki pasand”. A man in sunglasses and leather gloves tips the sachet into his mouth, so consumption is shown. It ends on the “Raj Niwas Flavoured Pan Masala” pack shot with a small line of text saying chewing pan masala is harmful to health, not for minors, and 0% tobacco. The main message makes the pan masala brand attractive and shows it being used, so I labelled it promotional

A_0005.why: “Dilbagh Pan Masala - TVC by Basic Communications”, 15 sec, a TV commercial for Dilbagh Royal Pan Masala posted by the ad agency. A man in a dark suit enjoys a meal at a restaurant, then tips a pan masala sachet into his mouth, so consumption is shown. It ends on a pack shot of "दिलबाग रॉयल पान मसाला" against a golden glitter background. A small on-screen warning reads “Chewing of pan masala is injurious to health, not for minors” throughout. The main message makes the brand attractive and shows the product being used, so I labelled it promotional. The small required warning does not change that.

A_0006.why: “Shikhar Pan Masala TVC”, about 60 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel. A cinematic film of a man in a suit with a car on a coastal road, a desert, an engineer in a hard hat at sunset, a wind turbine and a village lit up at night. It ends on a pack shot of “Shikhar Pan Masala” with the tagline "जो दिल की सुनते हैं, वो शिखर पर रहते हैं". The main message links the pan masala brand to ambition, success and progress, so it makes the brand attractive. A small on-screen line says chewing pan masala is injurious to health, contains 0% tobacco and is not for minors. This required warning does not change the main message, so I labelled it promotional.

A_0007.why: “Ganesh Pan Masala TVC”, about 36 sec, a Tamil-language TV commercial for Ganesh 701 scented supari / pan masala, uploaded by a film production channel (Yaanus Films). The title card reads “GANESH 701 Scented Supari – 30 sec Tamil 11.09.09”. A man in a black leather jacket and sunglasses holds up a yellow Ganesh 701 sachet while a festive crowd cheers around him. The closing Tamil line on screen reads "பெயரே கேட்டாலே சும்மா அதிருதில்ல" (just hearing the name sends a thrill), shown with the Ganesh 701 logo. The main message makes the brand exciting and attractive through a celebrity-style hero and crowd energy. I saw no health warning in the frames I checked, so I labelled it promotional.

A_0008.why: “Dilbagh Pan Masala Diwali TVC”, 10 sec, a Diwali greeting commercial uploaded by the ad agency (Basic Communications). A "दिलबाग रॉयल पान मसाला" pack is shown throughout, with fireworks and diyas appearing around it. The Hindi voiceover and subtitles say "दिलबाग की तरफ से आप सभी को दीपावली की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं" and end with the slogan "दिलबाग पान मसाला, दिल है तो जोश है". A small on-screen line says chewing pan masala is injurious to health and not for minors. The main message ties the brand name and slogan to a festive greeting, which makes the brand attractive

A_0009.why: “Goa Pan Masala | #kamyabikikick | TVC (45 sec) | Sanjay Dutt, Ravi Kishan & Krushna Abhishek”, 45 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel (Goa Pan Masala). A comedy-style celebrity ad: a man in a blue blazer and sunglasses talks to the camera and puts a Goa sachet to his mouth, other men talk next to a sports car, and a shopkeeper holds up a sachet. It ends on a pack shot with the line “Oonchi Khushboo.. Ooncha Swad..!” and price bursts of ₹10 and ₹5. The description names the three film stars and the campaign “Kamyabi Ki Kick”. The main message makes the brand attractive through star power, humour and a low price, and shows the product being used. I saw no health warning in the frames I checked, so I labelled it promotional.

A_0010.why: This is a 60-second TVC (MATES upload) for Pan Vilas Pan Masala, starring Manoj Bajpayee. It opens on a heritage mansion with the on-screen text “PAN VILAS – NAWAB”. It then shows the lead in a cream kurta in a period “Nawabi” setting: a man reading a newspaper headed “Second Innings”, rooftop scenes with attendants holding an umbrella, and a hall full of people. The Hindi subtitles are fragmentary. They include "गांव में", "दूध वाले को चाय तक पापा कम हो तो" and "है और", plus [संगीत] music cues. The ad builds an aspirational, royal, premium image around the Pan Vilas brand and a celebrity face, which makes the product attractive. There is no warning or discouragement in any frame I sampled (2s, 12s, 22s, 32s, 42s, 52s, 62s, 66s), and the last frame at 69s is black. I did not check the exact end-card frame, so a small legal or health line there is possible. It would not change the label, because the main message sells the product and normalizes its use.

B_0008.why: This is a 30-second Indian public-health PSA from Vital Strategies. The description says it ran in 2020 to support the ban on spitting and on smokeless tobacco in public places, and it urges people to quit tobacco to fight COVID-19. It opens in a village tea stall, where a man in a pink shirt sits among others. Then comes a rural courtyard scene with a woman cooking and a man in a yellow shirt. In a doctor’s clinic, a patient in a cream shirt, with a doctor facing him, repeats the English-subtitled line “I don’t believe that tobacco kills.” That line is then undercut by a graphic, red-toned close-up of an operation, with the subtitle “that tobacco kills. Some people…”. After that, the same man lies in a hospital bed in a white sheet, with his wife, an older woman and a young girl in a yellow top standing beside him. The ad ends on a black end card reading “QUIT TOBACCO – FIGHT CORONAVIRUS”, with the toll-free quitline “1-800-11-2356”, a missed-call number “011-22901701”, and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and National Tobacco Control Programme logos. The closing subtitle says “Quit tobacco and stay healthy to fight coronavirus.” The whole message warns about harm, discourages use and supports quitting, and nothing in it makes tobacco attractive.

B_0009.why: This is a 36-second anti-smoking TVC from Vital Strategies about secondhand smoke. Its title card reads “VITAL STRATEGIES – ANTI SMOKING TVC (SICKENING) – 30 SEC – ENGLISH – 01.03.17”. The first scene is a doctor’s consultation. A woman in a red saree sits at a desk, and the English auto-subtitle reads “he’s having trouble…”. Next, a shirtless teenage boy is examined as the subtitles say “he’s having trouble breathing, let’s take a look during an asthma…”. The next frames show him wincing and holding his chest as the subtitles explain that the muscles around the airways tighten and swell. Then come “uncontrollable coughing and difficulty breathing”. The ad ends on a black end card with the text “TOBACCO KILLS – QUIT TODAY!” and a no-smoking sign over a smouldering ashtray, with the logos of the health ministry and Vital Strategies. The last subtitle, “smoking around others is sickening, quit today”, gives the main message that smoking harms other people and that smokers should quit. The ad shows no attractive use of tobacco, so it is purely a warning that discourages use.

B_0010.why: This is a 30-second Hindi anti-smoking PSA. The video description says the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with technical support from World Lung Foundation, launched the “Artery” campaign in January 2014 to warn about smoking damage to the heart. It opens on a close-up of a man’s hand, with a gold ring, holding a cigarette. Next, a man in a light shirt stands on a street beside a sign reading “PLEASE THROW USED CIGARETTE BUTTS IN WHITE BUCKET”. The ad then cuts to a surgical-style scene in which gloved hands on a green cloth hold a reddish artery. The next close-ups show the artery clogged with yellow fatty plaque, and then the plaque lifted out beside the artery. A dark smoke shot follows. The ad ends on a black end card with the Hindi text "तम्बाकू जानलेवा है – आज ही छोड़ो" (“Tobacco is deadly – quit today”), a no-smoking sign, and the logos of the health ministry and the National Tobacco Control Programme. The message links smoking to damaged arteries and death and urges viewers to quit. The cigarette in the opening only sets up the harm, and nothing in the ad makes smoking attractive

B_0011.why: This is a 36-second Hindi anti-tobacco PSA (“I Don’t Believe”, 05.10.16) issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Tobacco Control Programme. Village men sit talking, and one of them repeats «मैं नहीं मानता कि तंबाकू जानलेवा है». A graphic surgical close-up follows, and then the same man lies in a hospital bed with a worried girl and an older woman beside him. A voice says «चाहे हम कुछ भी कहें, कुछ लोग हमारा संदेश नहीं सुनते», and the ad closes with «तंबाकू जानलेवा है। यह चेतावनी हर पैक पर है। इसे पढ़िए और इस पर विश्वास कीजिए». The end card shows a smokeless tobacco pouch inside a prohibition sign, with the text «तम्बाकू जानलेवा है – इसे पढ़िए». It warns about the harm and discourages use, and nothing in it makes tobacco attractive.

B_0012.why: This is a 38-second Hindi anti-tobacco PSA from Vital Strategies. It opens on a title card reading “WHAT DAMAGE WILL THIS CIGARETTE DO – HINDI – 30 SEC – 290518”. Weathered hands open a pack of cigarettes, and the shots that follow show a man being spoon-fed by a woman beside the Hindi word «स्ट्रोक», and a man lying ill in a hospital bed. The ad then returns to the hands with the Hindi question in red and white, «यह सिगरेट या बीड़ी पीने का क्या परिणाम होगा?». The end card reads «तम्बाकू आज ही छोड़ें» next to a no-smoking sign, followed by «सहायता के लिए कॉल करें 1-800-11-2356 (टोल फ्री) या मिस्ड कॉल दें 011-22901701». The health ministry and National Tobacco Control Programme logos appear at the bottom. The ad links cigarette and bidi use to stroke and serious illness and urges viewers to quit with a helpline, so it warns about harm and discourages use. The cigarettes appear only to set up the harm, not to make smoking appealing.
